speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness; to begin our assessment, on a scale of one to ten, how would you rate the intensity of your pain? Additionally, can you tell me if your symptoms radiate down your arm or if they are localized only to the neck?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Radiculopathy.

Given your one-year history of burning pain, paresthesias, and recent progressive weakness in both hands, combined with your age and diabetes history, I need to assess your neurological status immediately. Can you tell me if you have experienced any difficulty with balance, frequent dropping of objects, or numbness in your groin area?
